# Calendar draft updates require a complete section patch

## Draft and baseline

`resetDraft()` clones starting values into `baseline`, clears dirty-section and validation data, then clones the baseline into `value`. The baseline and editable value are separate objects. The baseline identity also helps Save detect when a draft was replaced.

`setSectionValidity()` clones a supplied validation result into the matching session. It does nothing when the session is absent. This action does not save a calendar event.

## Updating a section

`updateSection()` requires an existing editable draft and a non-null object patch that is not an array. It clones the patch. For enabled-row flags, it merges the supplied flags with retained flags before assigning values.

It then decides whether the section is dirty by comparing the supplied keys with baseline values. Enabled-row flags are compared only for the supplied rows. It adds or removes the section name from `dirtySections`.

The caller must supply all draft properties owned by the section, including unchanged values. The reducer cannot infer a changed property omitted from a patch. An incomplete patch can remove the section from the dirty list even while another property in that section still differs. This is an explicit caller contract stated in the source.

## Applying an edit

`applyCalendarEventDraft()` changes the event title only when the draft differs from the baseline. It treats start and end independently, preserves unchanged provider values, and sets null for a changed missing date.

For a whole-series edit that started from an occurrence, it shifts the parent date by the difference between the requested date and that occurrence's date. It then preserves the requested all-day flag and timezone. For an occurrence edit or an ordinary event, it uses the requested date directly.

This function does not validate dates or choose which live occurrence to edit. Its caller must supply the correct mutable event, baseline, and live occurrence. The full edit queue and recurrence selection need a separate behavior review.

## Evidence and limits

This note describes the code at `87d0159c7149a43253964c2cb6917939557dc799`. Read the named functions with `git show 87d0159c7149a43253964c2cb6917939557dc799:path` in a source clone. Function names are stable anchors; line ranges belong to the accompanying syntax maps. The implementation and named callers were read. No product build or runtime test ran for this study. The note does not prove every branch works, establish a style rule, or explain historical intent beyond reasons stated in the source. The source clone must contain this commit; a shared knowledge clone does not include the source itself.
